formTitle: DV-140 Child Custody and Visitation Order
_comment: DV-140 is a court order - it says so at the foot of every page - and it is attached to DV-110. The split is DV-110's: the filer supplies items 1, 2 and 3, which is the identifying part, and every other field is the judge's and is marked courtUse, so no question is ever generated for it. The filer's fields share the packet's names where the packet already has the answer, so the children named on DV-105 are the children printed here. The court's fields are named from their XFA path - meaningless but unique and stable, and nobody has to read them because nothing asks about them.

fields.label: 3. Children under 18 years old
fields._why: The box beside the item number on a court order marks the section the judge is granting, not a fact the filer supplies - the children themselves are named below it and those are the filer's.

fields.label: 3. More children listed on a separate page
fields._why: The same box DV-105 prints, asked once there.

_sharedNote: Items 1 and 2 ask the two relationships DV-105 already asks, so they carry DV-105 names and one answer fills both forms. Item 3 carries DV-105 child names for the same reason. That leaves DV-140 asking nothing at all - like DV-109, it is a form the packet fills entirely from what it already knows.
